# `get_solve_obj`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Read the star positions from the existing plate-solve intermediate file and return three values per row.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit and 32-bit builds) |
| Side-effect tier | D |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xb2ef0, GetObjFromAxy @0x15efa0, data_from_fit @0x15d220 (64-bit build) |

Reads the first four columns of at most 100 rows from the solver's intermediate table file in the device temporary directory and returns three of the four values per row. It starts no solve; with no or unsuitable file it fails with 207. The rows are stars detected in the last solve image, from the solver's source-extraction table; the three values are its first, second and fourth columns, taken to be x, y (pixels) and background (INFERRED).

Side effects: Reads existing FITS table data into request-local buffers. A reachable unsuitable-HDU branch of the reader calls a diagnostic print routine (INFERRED to write to standard output), which is why the grade is MUTATOR. The matching FITS-library bodies are not resolved, so the observer tier stays D. File parsing can block; no explicit timeout.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"get_solve_obj"`. [READ] |
| `params` | any | no | - | Not read. Omission, null, object, scalar and array all take the same path. Clients SHOULD omit it. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (both) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | (get_solve_obj success reply) The request method, echoed. [READ] |
| `result` | array<array<number>> | yes | - | (get_solve_obj success reply) Rows read from the existing solve-result file, at most 100. The handler computes the row count as list length divided by the reported FITS column count while the helper copies exactly four values per row, so a file wider than four columns can reduce the emitted count. [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (get_solve_obj success reply) Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (get_solve_obj success reply) Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |

| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 207 | The helper failed (needs more than 3 columns and more than 0 rows) or the reported column count is below 4 | `fail to operate` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

No result member is present on error.

## Example

Request, get:

```json
{"id":91,"method":"get_solve_obj"}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_solve_obj","result":[[512,384,20],[100,700,15]],"code":0,"id":91}
```

Reply, no-data:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_solve_obj","error":"fail to operate","code":207,"id":92}
```
